title: Reading the Financial Statements of a Regulated Firm
summary: Plain-language guide to the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, and how they look different for banks, investment firms, payment firms, fund managers and insurers.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Plain-language guide to the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, and how they look different for banks, investment firms, payment firms, fund managers and insurers.
Learning Objectives: Explain how the three primary statements connect
Recognise the distinctive features of different regulated business models
Identify the lines in the accounts that matter most to supervisors
Syllabus: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow: how they fit together
Business model differences: lending, dealing, payments, asset management and insurance
Client money and assets: why they sit apart from the balance sheet
Notes to the accounts: where the important information hides
Intended Audience: Non-executive and independent directors without a finance or accounting background
Chairs and members of board committees other than audit, and newly appointed directors
Executive directors and senior managers from non-finance functions who sign off plans or returns
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No accounting or finance qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Basel Framework (consolidated Basel III standards)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
